subject: Business
title: Pivoting: When to Change Direction
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pivoting: When to Change Direction.

hook.text: Slack started as a video game company. The game flopped, but the internal chat tool they built became worth $27 billion.

buildup.text: A pivot means changing strategy while keeping what you've learned. It's not failure — it's informed redirection.

discovery.text: Types of pivots: customer segment, value proposition, channel, revenue model, technology, and platform.

twist.text: The hardest part of pivoting is admitting the original idea isn't working. Ego and sunk costs delay the decision.

climax.text: YouTube started as a video dating site. Instagram started as a check-in app. Twitter started as a podcast platform.

punchline.text: The plan you start with is almost never the plan that works. Adapt.

quiz.question: What is a business pivot?
options: Changing strategy while keeping what you've learned

details.summary: A pivot is a structured course correction where a startup changes its strategy while keeping what it has learned. Instagram pivoted from a location check-in app called Burbn, Slack from a gaming company, and YouTube from a video dating site, finding their real market through iteration.
details.whyItMatters: Most successful startups pivot at least once. Knowing when to change direction versus persist with the current strategy is one of the hardest and most consequential decisions an entrepreneur faces during a company's early life.
takeaways: A pivot changes strategy while preserving validated learning from past efforts
Instagram, Slack, and YouTube all pivoted to find their successful markets
The decision between pivoting and persisting requires honest data assessment

faq.question: How do you know when it is time to pivot?
faq.answer: Key signals include consistently declining engagement metrics despite iterations, inability to achieve product-market fit after significant effort, discovering that a side feature generates more excitement than the core product, and running out of runway to test the current hypothesis.

faq.question: What is the difference between a pivot and giving up?
faq.answer: A pivot applies learning from failed approaches to a new direction. Giving up discards everything. Pivots preserve team, technology, customer insights, and domain expertise while redirecting them toward a more promising opportunity that the original effort helped reveal.
